problems.problem: Rule 2: the plain-sense clause ‘Mocked by Beth-el’s children, Elisha curses them and bears maul forty-two’ retells the key verse line by line (the curse, the two she-bears, the forty-two) instead of giving context; the key verse is printed just above, so the reader meets the same event twice and learns nothing of where it stands (2:23, the jeering on the way up to Beth-el).
problems.fix: Replace the context clause with the lead-in from 2:23 and keep the reading unchanged: ‘On the way to Beth-el, children from the city mock Elisha; Radak, on 2:24, explains that the sages, troubled by the deaths, gave reasons, as that he saw no trace of a commandment in them or their seed, and said he was punished with illness.’ (45 words; entry-check ok on scratch/critic/fix-d117.json).

problems.problem: Prose: the context clause doubles itself, ‘Answering Michal ... David replies’, so the opening says the same thing twice.
problems.fix: ‘Rebuked by Michal, who scorns his dancing before the ark, David answers her; Radak, on 6:22, reads it as lowering himself before God, no disgrace but honour, since making light of himself for God’s honour makes him honoured in the eyes of all.’ (43 words; entry-check ok on scratch/critic/fix-d098.json).
